channel.title: Stefan Langenbach
channel.description: Monthly learnings, podcast picks and the occasional find from around the web.

item.title: Cult Repo tech documentaries
item.description: I first discovered Cult Repo through the Node JS and Python documentaries back in 2024 and 2025. What I didn’t know, was that they have been creating software related documentaries (Kubernetes, Prometheus, Ruby, etc.) since 2018. Their most recent movies are about C++ and Java’s Spring Boot Framework. And although I never was a C++, nor Java developer, I really enjoyed both movies.

item.title: Pi, Data-Intensive Applications and OpenCode
item.description:
TL;DR

  • Building Pi with Mario Zechner and Armin Ronacher
  • Designing Data-Intensive Applications with Martin Kleppmann
  • Building OpenCode with Dax Raad

Building Pi

I really liked this episode from the Pragmatic Engineer Podcast. Mario’s approach to building a simple, stable and reliable coding agent is a very welcome breath of fresh air in the overhyped AI coding tools landscape.

Designing Data-Intensive Applications

Martin Kleppmann’s book Designing Data-Intensive Applications is considered a classic in software development literature. I personally own a copy and am currently reading through it. While it was great to hear that Martin has published the second edition of the book, his thoughts regarding local-first software really caught my interest. If you want to find out more about the local-first concept, check out Cult Repo’s mini documentation:

Building OpenCode

A great look behind the scenes of developing OpenCode, combined with a realistic take on using AI for software development.

item.title: The AI Doc
item.description: In his recent conversation with Sam Harris, Tristan Harris, which you might recall from The Social Dilemma, discusses the documentary The AI Doc. The movie investigates the risk and opportunities of AI by interviewing various researchers, CEOs and staff of the major AI labs. AFAIK the move is not yet available online, but the trailer already looks great.

item.title: DHH, Mitchell Hashimoto, Building Claude Code, Wetware and Monty
item.description:
I have been an avid podcast listener for more than a decade. When I began listening, the podcast world was small: I was subscribing to a handful of indie podcasts focusing on technology, journalism, nonsense and everything in between. Episodes were released occasionally and it was easy to keep up with the shows. Today, podcasts are everywhere, and it’s much harder to keep up. The Favorite Podcast Episodes series is an attempt to recommend episodes actually worth listening to.

TL;DR

  • DHH on PE (c.f. DHH on Lex Friedman)
  • Mitchell Hashimoto on PE
  • Building Claude Code with Boris Cherny on PE
  • Last Invention: New episode on Wetware and an interview with Sam Altman’s attacker
  • Monty: Python in Rust for AI with Samuel Colvin on Talk Python To Me

DHH on PE

Conversations with David Heinerman Hanson (DHH) are always worth listening to. In this episode on the Pragmatic Engineer’s (PE) podcast, DHH talks about his journey agentic engineering journey.

Mitchell Hashimoto on PE

Another feature from the PE podcast with Mitchel Hashimoto about the history of Hashicorp, the attitude of major cloud providers, how he uses AI and Ghostty.

Building Claude Code

An interview with the core developer of Claude Code - especially interesting because of the recent Claude Code leak.

Last Invention: Wetware

Another episode from the excellent Last Invention podcast on biological computers.

Monty

Samuel Colvin discusses Monty, a Python interpreter for AI agents written in Rust.

item.title: Quarto, Small Language Models, Self-Hosting
item.description:
TL;DR

Use Quarto for presentations and documents; If you’re hardware allows it, run small language models locally using Ollama. Give the latest iteration of Gemma a try; Seriously consider self-hosting if you have basic Linux and DevOps experience. A Linux server, reverse-proxy and container runtime is all you need to get started.

Quarto

Experimenting with Quarto has been on my list for a long time. This month I finally got to use it to create revealjs powered slides and a typst based document. I authored both documents in VSCode using the official Quarto extension and won’t go back.

Small Language Models

With the release of Gemma 4, I’ve updated my Ollama installation and took several small, open-source language models (Granite 4, Qwen 3.5, Gemma 4 and SmolLM v3) for a ride. My current hardware setup (MacBook Air M2 with 16 RAM) only allows me to run the tiny versions of those models. While all of them work great for prototyping AI-powered applications, they don’t yet replace frontier models for more advanced tasks. I might just need to invest in beefier hardware to make that happen.

Selfhosting

I went down the self-hosting and homelab rabbit hole after reading Michael Kennedy’s Talk Python in Production book. After researching self-hosted PaaS solutions, I tinkered with disco on a super cheap Hetzner server to host apps over at byteCare. Currently, I am implementing a custom solution based on Caddy, Docker Compose and Zitadel. Stay tuned, this might deserve its own blog post.

item.title: The Last Invention
item.description: I stumbled upon a gem last week: The Last Invention from Longview is a podcast series about the origins, development, risks and opportunities posed by AI. Starting with the Turing test in the 1950s, it goes on to tell the story of AI development, mentioning DeepBlue, Watson, AlphaGo, Deepmind, OpenAI and Anthropic. During the last week, I listened to the entire first season and can only recommend it: It’s thought-provoking, very well produced and just fascinating.

item.title: Hello World
item.description:
Dear reader,

welcome to my blog.

This is my second? attempt at publishing content regularly. The plan is to use this blog to document the things I learned (TIL). As I have a life outside work, I won’t do so on daily basis. Instead, my goal is create one post per month featuring the most important learnings. I promise not to use AI to generate the text you will read. This is an exercise in writing, not AI engineering.

Looking forward to have you with me on this journey.
